title: Parts Discount and Alternate Parts Targets by Insurer Program Agreement Tier
content:
Two parts terms in the Insurer Program Agreements vary by tier:

- **Original-equipment parts discount** — the discount passed to the insurer on original-equipment parts list prices, in percent.
- **Alternate parts target** — the target share of aftermarket and recycled parts on eligible lines, in percent; 0 means no target.

| Agreement tier | Original-equipment parts discount | Alternate parts target |
|---|---|---|
| Network Referral Agreement | 0% | 0% |
| Select Direct Repair Agreement | 2% | 20% |
| Preferred Direct Repair Agreement | 3% | 25% |
| Premier Direct Repair Agreement | 4% | 30% |
| Managed Repair Program Agreement | 5% | 30% |
| Enterprise Master Services Agreement | 6% | 35% |

## Reading the two columns

The discount is a percentage of the original-equipment list price of a part. The target is a share of the eligible lines, measured across aftermarket and recycled parts together; it states an aim for the parts mix, not a price.

A Network Referral Agreement passes no discount on original-equipment parts (0%) and has no alternate parts target (0 means no target).

## Worked illustration (hypothetical part)

A hypothetical original-equipment bumper cover lists at 800.00. Under a Managed Repair Program Agreement the discount passed to the insurer is 5% of 800.00, which is 40.00; under a Select Direct Repair Agreement it is 2% of 800.00, which is 16.00; under a Network Referral Agreement it is nothing. The list price is invented for the illustration.

## Questions on the terms

**Does the discount apply to aftermarket or recycled parts?** The discount is stated on original-equipment parts list prices only.

**Do two tiers share the same alternate parts target?** Yes; the Premier Direct Repair Agreement and the Managed Repair Program Agreement both carry 30%.
